summary: Not an allocated object: this entry groups the B and C copies of a packed-byte 1:2:1 video post-filter kernel (now Video_FilterPackedBytesBlock2_B 0x0013F130 / _C 0x00145730). Its 'self' is the raw source frame buffer (byte* param_1), so the recorded offsets are source-frame sample positions rather than struct members.
evidence: Raw signature `void FUN_0013F130(byte *param_1,int *param_2,int param_3)` (the C copy FUN_00145730 has the same body on the doubled 0x200 pitch): every 32-bit word is masked with 0x7F7F7F7F so the 1:2:1 average cannot carry between the four packed byte lanes, four words are written to param_2 and four more one 0x100-byte (B) / 0x200-byte (C) row further per pass. No ctor, vtable, allocation or object-like access. struct_db multiplied the pointer index by 4, so each batch offset is 4 x the true byte offset; the R3 sweep renamed FilterRgba to FilterPackedBytes.
